transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I start projects excited, but I just can’t seem to follow through and finish assignments or client work on time unless there’s a crisis. It's gotten to the point where it's really hurting my classes and my freelance projects, and I just don't know how to break the cycle.
Did you experience these difficulties with focus and completing tasks during your childhood, or is this a relatively new development in your life?

These issues have actually been with me since childhood; back in elementary school, my teachers would write that I was "bright but daydreams and rushes," and my parents were often called in because I'd blurt out answers, fidget, and forget to turn in my homework. It has always been a constant background struggle for me, but it only became completely unmanageable over the past year and a half when my college workload and freelance projects ramped up.

Over the past year and a half, have you also been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or is your distress primarily related to the frustration of not getting tasks done?

My distress is definitely tied to the frustration of not being able to follow through and the constant fear of ruining my GPA and career. I actually still get really excited to start new projects, so it's not that I've lost interest or feel persistently sad. It's just deep frustration and anxiety about my performance and missed deadlines over the last year and a half.
